findings.title: Capitalisation indexes by UTF-16 code unit, so words starting with astral letters are not capitalised
findings.property: the first letter of each word in pascalSnakeCase output is uppercase when the letter has an uppercase form
findings.evidence: split() uses \p{L} with the u flag, so astral letters count as word letters, but capitalCaseTransformFactory does upper(word[0]) / word.slice(1), which cuts a surrogate pair in half; toUpperCase of a lone high surrogate is a no-op. Doc: 'Convert a string to pascal snake case (Foo_Bar)'.

Expected values to be strictly equal:

review.title: Capitalisation splits surrogate pairs, so words starting with astral cased letters are not capitalised
review.reason: The splitter uses \p{L} with the u flag, so an astral letter such as U+10428 is a valid word character. capitalCaseTransformFactory and pascalCaseTransformFactory then take word[0] and word.slice(1), which cut the surrogate pair in half. toUpperCase on a lone surrogate does nothing, so the first letter stays lowercase and the documented 'Foo_Bar' capitalisation is not applied. The input is valid and the repro is correct. A fix is small (use the first code point, e.g. String.fromCodePoint(word.codePointAt(0)) or Array.from), though the affected scripts (Deseret, Osage, Adlam and similar) are rare.
